title: Everyone called (Lumen Gentium 40)
hook: all are called to the fullness of Christian life
tomorrow: can Mary be a mother to us without taking from Christ?

segments.voice: Yesterday Lumen Gentium named the family, so to speak, the domestic church: the church at home, where faith is first heard.

Search the word saint and the images are halos, robes and folded hands: people who never seem to wait in a parking lot or fold laundry. So here's an odd detail. When Vatican II's document on the Church gets to holiness, it doesn't start with monks. It starts with Jesus asking for perfection from everybody: "Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect." Everybody? Perfect? That sounds like a setup for failure, unless the council means something else by perfect.
screen: `HALOS, ROBES, FOLDED HANDS.` → `BE YOU THEREFORE PERFECT.` → `EVERYBODY? PERFECT?`

segments.voice: Paragraph forty solves it in four moves. First, who's asked. Jesus, it says, preached holiness of life to each and every one of his disciples, whatever their condition. The chapter's title even uses the word universal: a universal call to holiness. Second, where holiness comes from. Not from people's own works, the paragraph says, but from God's purpose and grace. In baptism they're made children of God and truly holy. So the job isn't to manufacture holiness. It's to hold on to it and bring it to completion. Third, the honest part. The same paragraph admits that we all stumble in many things, so we need God's mercy every day, and we pray, forgive us our trespasses. So perfect here can't mean flawless. The call goes out to people who are still tripping. Fourth, the answer to the puzzle. All the faithful, of whatever rank or state, are called to the fullness of the Christian life and to the perfection of love. Perfect, in this paragraph, is measured in love. And the council adds a quiet line: holiness like this makes life on earth more human. The nurse on nights, the grandfather, the teenager, the bishop: one call, lived in different places.
screen: `EACH AND EVERY DISCIPLE.` · `HOLY BY GRACE, NOT BY WORKS.` · `WE ALL STUMBLE, DAILY MERCY.` · `PERFECT, MEASURED IN LOVE.` · then, large: `ALL CALLED.`

segments.voice: Choose one ordinary hour from tomorrow: a class, a shift, a ride home. Name one loving thing you'd like to happen in it, and then the thing most likely to get in the way. Decide now what you'll do when that obstacle shows up, and rest with the plan while the timer runs.
Everyone called. Lumen Gentium's universal call: holiness, measured in love, for every baptized person.
Hold onto this: all called, the bishop and the teenager alike, including the ones still tripping. Until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1584 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: A MOTHER WHO TAKES NOTHING FROM HIM?`

howItsDone: Catholics speak of the universal call to holiness to mean that laypeople, in their work and family life, are called to holiness as fully as priests and religious, and parishes and lay movements build their teaching on it.

fork.setup: your coworker says she's given up on being "a good Catholic" because she keeps losing her temper in traffic. what does Lumen Gentium 40 offer her?
options: holiness is mostly for calmer people in religious life.
the call goes to people still stumbling; mercy is daily.
she has to stop losing her temper before she can begin.
fork.reveal: the paragraph admits we all stumble in many things and need mercy every day. the call to the perfection of love doesn't wait for anyone to be finished.

options: Kind of. Vatican II says every baptized person is called to holiness, kids too, right where they are.
Not really. Holiness is mainly for priests and nuns; the rest of us just try to be decent people.

chat.meaning: Lumen Gentium 40: all the faithful, of any state, are called to the fullness of Christian life and the perfection of love, and all need daily mercy.

Vatican II.meaning: the Second Vatican Council, a gathering of the world's Catholic bishops

Lumen Gentium.meaning: Vatican II's document on the Church; Latin for light of the nations

trespasses.meaning: an older word for sins, as in the Lord's Prayer

baptism.meaning: the sacrament of water that makes a person a Christian

notes: Lumen Gentium 40 paraphrased (official English not public domain): confirm 'preached holiness of life to each and every one of His disciples of every condition', 'called not according to their works, but according to His own purpose and grace', made holy in baptism and to hold on to and complete that holiness, 'in many things we all offend' and need mercy daily, praying 'forgive us our debts/trespasses', 'all the faithful of whatever rank or status are called to the fullness of the Christian life and to the perfection of charity', and 'a more human manner of living'.
LG 40 cites Matthew 6:12; the script uses 'forgive us our trespasses' as Catholics pray it, not a quotation of the council's translation (no quotation marks).
Chapter 5 title recalled as 'The Universal Call to Holiness in the Church'; confirm.
Matthew 5:48 quoted from Douay-Rheims; confirm exact wording.
